source_evidence: Exact player 'look through the sacks' authorizes opening and examining all three tied sacks in first worked chamber, not removing or transporting their contents. Day338~06:13–06:16 V and companions open and visually compare them. DM establishes mundane contents consistent with previously fixed silver-prospecting operation: first sack mostly coarse pale freshly broken host rock with sparse dark metallic-looking flecks, second sack denser hand-selected gray metallic-looking ore fragments, third sack smaller crushed and sorted pieces of similar metallic-looking material, more carefully separated from waste rock, no refined ingots or coins. Sacks marked with charcoal sorting symbols; Fenar matches the same Undercommon 'silver stone' label on the latter two, and 'poor stone' on the first. This supports a deliberate trial extraction and sorting process, not verified ore assay, grade, yield, weight, sale value, commercially viable deposit or proof of silver. All contents mundane as far as currently active Detect Magic can determine; no unfamiliar magic, documents, hidden compartment, magic item or creature discovered by this ordinary visual examination. No check needed for directly visible contents and straightforward known-language markings; no assay attempted. Contents stay in sacks in chamber, no loot or sample custody changed. No deeper passage entry, spell/feature expenditure, new damage, supplies consumed or other resource change. V chooses next action.
